q1_issues.issue: The top-level group "come" event (statements 1-2) carries no Result link and no result state, so at group level the parse asserts only that the cauldrons "came" — reading as motion — with "to a slow boil" recoverable solely from inside the per-member rule.

q2_gaps: light-verb change-of-state "come to a <state noun>" — the change-of-kind/phase rule names only "became" / "turned into" / "turned ADJ" and the idiom rule is a coherence test, so nothing decides between a fixed idiom symbol (come_to_a_boil) and the become-pattern the parse used; under that pattern the mandatory flat dual-emit yields (Member $x boil), i.e. each cauldron IS a boil
notes: Definite plural -> group plus per-member distribution rule, Patient on the change-of-state subject, and the absent tense atom on the bare simple present are all correct. Whether "a slow boil" licenses the Skolem-function state variant of the resultative group rule (reserved for states carrying their own per-member complement) is marginal — "slow" is a modifier, not a complement.
